Content: We start each day with breaths of gratitude and love.

In Southern California, all our cultures are our way to learn and understand. All our cultural ways are valued. These different ways are a way for us to stay connected to land. We took the best of our cultures and brought them together. There is a multi-racial way of being where we took the best of our cultures.

Water, land, and sky. All three are thriving, clean, and healthy. Mutual stewardship. Everyone knows how to water their own roots. Ceremonies and languages are thriving. Medicines are abundant and uninterrupted even in the cities. Education system is inclusive - decolonized. Safe homes for all. People experience elevation.

As people continue to need to move - migration has come to be seen more closely to the joy of who birds and animals migrate - humans no longer being separate. There is more ease - because good practices and protocols shape how we greet and meet each other. There is purpose in greetings. There is the first question - have you eaten? And the second questions - have you slept? And then - what might you need? Caution is present - wisdom has taught that - but hospitality leads.
We feel the spirit of Audre Lorde. Hands on the land / Reaching my heart forward / Greeting ancestors
That phrase, "I'm not an artist" doesn't exist. It's not a critique/perform culture. Creativity is embraced.

Cultures, experiences, spirit practices, healing practices are all so highly respected. Governance circles for community need are compiled based on the wisdom that exists in a community. No one person or people needs to have all the answers.
Art is supported in community- as a way to interrogate, dream, and excite.
Jazz concerts students have been doing. I hear and see a jazz combo.

Ceremony. Ahhh ceremony. There is the mundane and daily ceremony like the first time you reach the top branch of that tree you have been trying to reach and you run into your Uncle's arms to tell them about it and then there is the necessary healing ceremony. And then there is the baby is being born ceremony. And the welcoming the rain ceremony. Ceremony is not relegated to sundays. It is every day and on sacred sun/moon/star cycle days.
Cultural exchange happens joyfully and seamlessly. There are places where people learn from each other and share. People can be themselves and share freely.

Singing and chanting are a big part of our daily lives. We sing in celebration, we sing in praise, we sing when a child enters this world and we sing as we lay our loved ones to rest. We understand the healing power carried in the frequencies of our chants and songs. We each have a song in us...
Lots of music and singing. Marvel movie - the planet where everyone sings. Great grandma said there was a time when people didn't sing.
Art. People would feel the art first. It would deeply matter to the space. Artists would be supported. Art would capture the essence of places... and the past, present, future.
Music gets played and shared - easily.
We are a spirited peoples. We have many chants and many ways. And yet it is not cacophony.

We know how to bring ceremony to the everyday and we cultivate and cherish ways to honor the sacred. This includes the ways ancestors are seen and play with each of us. It includes the quiet spaces. Children see roles for spirit keepers and elders that they want to grow into. Our older ones are not in hiding or discarded. Even their most difficult dreams and delusions are held. Their late night tremors are met by loved ones. There is enough rest for each person the community and the resources for care are not transactions held by insurance companies - but the kind of insurance brought about in generational homes and villages. It isn't all easy - as we still struggle with families in conflict but there are ways to tend to changes in family the keep connections more whole rather than less. Part of the power of ceremony and song is to keep us finding ways to grow and be open and to choose to stay with it - to stay in the practice of caring for and being with Earth and Water and Sky and Bear and beloveds and niblings and ourselves.
Curiosity is valued above rightness. Joy! Echoing laughter. Playfulness.
Stories are abundant.
Shared sense of responsibility for one another’s well-being. More curiosity and holistic views.
Music is a way of being…and it teaches everyone. Song helps us communicate in a unified way.
There are rituals that give love and empathy to self and others for mistakes. We give and receive these in the course of a lifetime.

We know what to do when mistakes are made. When there is pain and when there is grieving there will be places to go. Everyone has access to the rituals, traditions, stories that help. Spirit nourishment is at the heart of every neighborhood and community. It is practices in spirit spaces, kitchens, back yards, homes, and any other place people gather.

We no longer just say sorry. Sorry is expressed through actions. It has a look, sound, feel, tast, smell etc. We learn across generations about how to do this. When harm is done, we talk about the harm, clean up the mess, and commit to not repeating the harm. When needed, there are community circles for healing and repairing. We accept and value everyone, and nourish self love and empathy even as we learn from mistakes.

We would have an infrastructure for creations – a way to catalog and be in relationship to them. People will have a shared library of creative works in their homes that they offer to others as part of a whole.

There will be so many murals on the walls. You will hear song and harmony when walking outside–along with the bubbling of the city's creeks. We will eat together and share the joy of nourishment together. Streets will be vibrant with life and energy.
There will still be Zines, D&D, and stories.
So many different kinds of language, food, and music are accessible and available.
Songs are savings accounts. Stories are the currency of the times. Wealth is a collective achievement.
People often wrap themselves in quilts. Quilts feel like the people that made them–and everyone is has at least one.
We learn and share knowledge not through 140 characters or Tik Tok - knowledge transfer is slow, intentional, from an Elder.
We learn to slow down and appreciate nature, family, and live in balance.
We live in regard, care, concern, and attunement.
Our stories are recorded via paintings and oral traditions.
The songs of the people remain in a way that keeps story and new songs emerge as a gift to the future.
People communicate lovingly and telepathically because global consciousness has evolved.
We make music and laugh and sing together. Art and creative process are part of daily life. Connection to spirit is primary and healing is part of sacred practice.

We are all wearing clothes that play homage to the skies – that shift in color as the light emerges; crimson red, then tangerine, midnight blue shifts to a dusty pink, a shimmering and rippling as the sun lifts entirely from the horizon, a pale blue brightening as ancient grains bubble on the stove, a uniform that reminds each other of the currency of color, of possibility, of awe.
Capitalism no longer exists nor democracy - no westernized teachings as the only way.

People know that movement connects us all. There are deep ways of practicing that connection. Being here by being seen. I see you. Sowubona. I am here. Ngikhona. Hand to one’s heart then to the ground of those who brought the music.

We continue to be inspired by stories of ancient Athenian society where people would dance, participate in theater and read/write poetry with a sense of creation in life–not just doing work to get through. People would live into “I was the janitor so you could be the doctor, I was the doctor so you can be the artist, etc.”
There are ceremonies to mark life transitions across life stages.
There is a new 4th of July Ceremony - The story of how the people learned to listen to the water. The ceremony follows the river. People know the plants and practices that make water thrive.

There is a ceremony for acknowledging the harm that has happened…the harm that has been caused, and what we are responsible for the following year. It happens in water, and is led by teenagers for adults and younger kids.

There is a quaker-type way of holding space, silence, and decision-making that honors everyone’s perspective. This is used within the communities and between communities. There’s a universal translator that allows people to communicate easily :-)

We have an annual ceremony in which we remember the way things used to be before, when isms reigned and harm was omnipresent. We do so not to celebrate defeating that way of being but to remember where we have been and where we do not wish to return.
People have joy - they sing, make music, dance, draw, paint. All of these things are appreciated.
We will practice recognizing similarities in our practices, wisdom, joy etc.

We will practice love moment by moment. When we don’t act with love, we will be accountable with each other. There will be clear and kind communication about what has gone wrong. We will be good at understanding where another person is coming from. We will have learned how to have our entire being tuned to this way of loving, caring, and being responsible for one another.
Shelter, food, education, and healthcare will be basic rights. People will be free to search for what they are meant to do.
Play has helped us build connection with one another–and has supported our journey to the horizon.
An eternal party. More time to enjoy cultural expressions
Original of Translation: Una fiesta eterna. Más tiempo para disfrutar las expresiones culturales.

Content: It becomes necessary for every human to practice a pause, a meditation, to find their souls again, day after day after day. To find their soul in connection to all others in the space between the earth and the sky. Our souls are connected, our roots in the earth. No one breaks the bonds.
One bowl and one spoon is practiced everywhere.

People will still be making journal entries. They will still choose to do it with pen and paper. People are awake and aware. Journal entries have so much description of the people we share life with, things to be done, work accomplished.
Journal entries from any week would include vibrant descriptions of community, collective thinking and action, big hearts, abundant sharing, capacity to hold, compassion, and deep love.
I see golden waves – with a road. Vibrant greens, blues, ocean, and sky. We start gathering with silence. We begin work with silence. We know how to connect and let our hearts guide all that we do.

Ownership:  The boundaries of ownership are blurred.  We take responsibility for what we are capable of being responsible for – and our  responsibility extends beyond my boundaries.  Every decision we make for the particular is informed by things that are way beyond.

Everyone knows how to be in the flow of energy…so energy workers aren’t a specific category of people.  There is the auntie who has helped a lot of people with arthritis.  There’s the uncle who helps when it’s especially hard to shake grief.  It is common to see the telltale signs that neighbors, friends, and colleagues are tending to energy.  Rituals, chanting, hands outstretched, moments of silence, and a strength and setness that a rotating majority walks with at any given time.
Value art +cultural world to build

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: Creating spaces for people to sit together;  realizing that we are stronger together. The young people don’t want to fight. When someone shares their story with you, it becomes a part of you. Listening to young people.

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: Taking care of others. Sharing love and connection of nature with others, especially young people and nephews.

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: Purple, playfulness

People do jobs that benefit all, and that are aligned with what they feel called to do. Art is not a hobby, but a way of life. We do our work artfully, we tend to our loved ones artfully and intentionally, we play artfully, we eat artfully. We dance a lot. Music is everywhere. Greenspaces aren’t set aside, but we fashion our dwellings and shelters in harmony with nature.

Inside coffee shops, people order in the language that feels like home to them. And the shop workers understand because everyday at the end of their shifts, they can join the circles of people living easy lives in the commons who learn each other’s languages with curiosity and joy.
Children aspire to pursue their art. Pro sports continues, but has changed drastically since safety measures were put in place and gambling disappeared.

Museums abound. Communities treasure the places that hold  memory of times past. Every community holds several museums, some of which highlight the good, others which offer an honest reckoning with the bad.

Everyone carries around their own cups for the multiple cups of tea, coffee, water they will share with others throughout the day.  If someone breaks their cup – they have been given at least 5 hand made replacements by the next day–which they, in turn, give away as needed or as joyful admiration dictates.
What religion there is centers the Maternal Divine.

Every day in our personal and community relationships, there is a space for “tell me your dream. How will you live it today? What resources do you need to reach it?” This changes the kind of knowledge that we value. We relate to one another through our dreams and where there is resonance with that and introducing each other to those who may know something to resource those dreams.

Beauty supplies are abundant. Libraries of adornment. Spaces where people can invite each other to do each others’ hair in public space, as a way to deepen relationships. There is time to do those things. Ceremonies for mutual appreciation.
The folktales, metaphors and sayings are reclaimed as part of our education and spiritual practices.

People will look back at what we thought we knew–at the grief we had in our loss, and empathise, honor, and celebrate it.  There will be celebrations to honor that what felt like total destruction was actually a birth.

We hear mahjong tiles clacking on what used to be the bart gliding by.  It's still a way people get from one place to another, but it’s also a gathering place for games and connection.  People enjoy the moving platform that gives sweeping views of the city.
There are more libraries and cultural centers that focus on fun and educational, and cultural programming for people of all ages.
Music fills the air, and spontaneous dancing and celebration is a real thing.
Lots of games and fun
The flea markets are poppin and the primary ways clothing, technology, tools, music, art are redistributed
We support the arts / the arts are heavily valued so everyone can access and participate in their own way / there’s always music
There are lots of museums. They are full of guns and military technologies. It is an ancient history, almost impossible to believe.
We made a song together that night, with the birds and frogs and whipping wind.

We wear Royal blues, dyed by flowers grown in our auntie sisters cousins garden, hand woven whites, embroidered with languages from tribes around the world along the seams. Tall in stature, stately and graceful in their movement. Their entrances quieted the space and then their laughter filled it right back up again.
We  sit on homemade cushions of bamboo and wheatgrass, poured what they called grown folks drank into handmade cups, decorated in mosaic tiles from every continent across the world. Collection items from their collective travels.
As the children adjusted to the majesty of their presence, their great great great great grandmother arrived, a screen floating in air coordinated by the same light and led technology that helped coordinate communication after the fall. The lights lit up, and they listened to the recording that told them the story of the dream she had that they would always make it here.”

Morning shows take place in corner stores and coffee shops. They open with a poem, where headlines are what types of edible plants are in season,   and young people are celebrated for their work at school. It’s comfortable, not slick, no one is selling anything.

My name is Uta (Japanese for song). I am the leader of songs in our sweet sea village, Salt Point.  I’m not really a good song voice in our village, but I loooove music!  I open the space and support for all villagers to sing, play their instruments, listen to one another in everyday gatherings… alone, in pairs, trios, and whole choruses and choirs!

Music creates the rhythms, beats, harmony, synchronicity (and even asynchronicity) that creates jazz.

The elders share the same past/ historical ways and stories that tell about the roots of music, especially jazz, invented in this continent by the mix of freedom songs from those who were enslaved, mixed with the people’s melodies, rhythms, and beats from the continents of Africa, South America, Asia, and Europe.  

Elders also shared that before the time of the collapse, people called singers and musicians “stars” and even “superstars.”  When these folx shared their songs, it was called “performances.”
Now in 2175, we enjoy listening and making music, yet of course everyone in the village shares and makes music as a part of our everyday practice and joy.  Performance is not who we are!
Art is re-integrated into life.
We are connected and recognizable to each other through practices that aren’t the same but bridge us.
We understand that music is as much about listening as it is making noise.
Art is still exciting because people step outside the norms.
Velvet cacti creation: A new performance group is created in town, called “The Transplants”. Each member of the group represents different wacky plants; They make art and discuss the new world.
Freedom to practice cultural expression(s).
Religions are peaceful and admiring of each other, at a fundamental level.
People work much less and have more time to play in nature and with art and music
In a more travelled world, we find ways to celebrate the ancient cultural meaning of each of the parts of the world without losing their uniqueness
Our songs, art, stories support all of us to be in right relationship with one another.

We have found new ways of sharing music with each other through song, rhyme and traditional means. There is a resource available – a library of all music ever made. It can be accessed the same way people access books – in a way that is ethically and most energetically aligned with the earth.

Religion is respected across all different cultures. We honor each other and our differences. We do that in song. The lessons we have learned always center the land and our relationship to the land. It has created such a healthy space for us to communicate, share our feelings.

We sing, write letters, dance under open skies. The internet has quieted, and social media is gone—replaced by conversation, art, and ceremony. Our elders and children guide us. We remember our histories honestly and use their lessons to shape a liberated now.
We nurture art, beauty, music, writing, and creativity. Many of us communicate through spirit, music, and movement. Artists and musicians are the most revered profession.
Beauty is not about design or fashion but about human essence. Art is expression of our reverence for each other and this planet and the mystery of life.

The timeplace of far horizon… there is a pluralistic sense of renewal. In Christian communities, everyone observes Holy Saturday, the day we do not know. The promise of renewal w/out the proof. There are rituals.

In the Sukkah, rabbis train the b’nei mitzvah youth on how to query the Golen- the Yiddish speaking AI the community builds and uses to guide it’s future. After the lesson they eat with their community fattoush, biryani, cornbread. They drink locally distilled slivovitz and laugh all night,

We have returned to Gaza for the annual festival of life. Trains arrive from all over Africa + the Levant. Palestinians from across the homeland + beyond attend to experience joy and abundance. Meals of fish + vegetables are shared. Poetry, dance, art & donkey fashion shows entertain.
Violence is no longer our chosen form of entertainment. We gather for music, theatre, and storytime.

The soil is clean because we all remember that it is not a given, the air is clean for the same reason. We remember. There are fewer of us. We have grief rituals of what we were that help us be present with what we are in another way. We remember, when we see ruins, that so many people loved us enough to make sure we kept going.
Music, dance, gardening and all sorts of extra opportunities are available to all.

We are on our way – a regression towards new society that gives me hope
Letting go towards peaceful identities
The flora and tapestries are brightly colored and represent the cycles of lives.

• Remember your culture, your traditions
• Freedom that doesn’t depend on a single language
• Dance
• Food

During celebrations and parties, there are poetry performances, singing, and music. People spend time together and connect, experiencing the joy of life together. When you walk into a party, the thrum of the music settles in your ribcage. Inside, you are greeted by your friends with hugs and kind words. You stop by the food table, getting some tacos with black eyed peas and plenty of salsa. You listen to the live band, the lead singer’s melodic voice echoing throughout the room. You feel at peace and happy.
Respect for every culture in each country of the world.
Clothes are simpler and more standard with comfortable shoes.
More drum circles, feeling and connecting to mother earth and father sun.
Our literature is shaped around new narratives that come from nature and the natural word.  We see the cooperation, collaboration, and symbiosis in our literature and metaphors.

Music is a more broadly spoken language. Houses are smaller because people gather in public spaces. At a night time event in a community space/battery storage event, instruments are shared and people come on stage and share from their different, personalized cultures and styles. Everyone feels connected to what’s happening as lines are connected from past to others. Unsupervised kids running around everywhere. Entertainment is active. Everyone is interested because they feel like they have a role, a sense of belonging. Everyone has more leisure time. We have the time to learn from each other.

Culture is how everyone expresses themselves on a daily basis. We are always in music and art. That changes how our living places look, how food growing looks, the way we engage in work is colored by artistry, through out movement and what we express verbally.

The value of handmade, human-generated, hand-crafted, culturally significant arts, music, foods, experiences, written documents, etc. becomes highly valued, as machine-generated objects become commonplace. The arts, literature, and creativity are celebrated and flourish as a counterpoint to technology.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Give more people awareness of the culture related to how Hawaiʻi can be self-reliant, rather than relying on imported goods that we may not have forever
People are encouraged to share and exchange cultures, backgrounds, experiences
Late nights filled with sounds mahjong shuffling, children laughing, eating spam musubi
We ritualize joy and local celebrations that are multicultural and at the level of mardi gras
Dance and music are part of public space
Fusion in cuisines language music
Music is created, carried and passed on by the people, inspired by the beauty of their world.
No one “owns” songs - they are recognized as gifts from spirit that benefit all beings.
Movement, breath, bird song, insects, and spiders are sacred–as is laughter and music.

There are open spaces and a field of different grasses in the middle of town.  I see everyone gathered there, in different stages of arrival, all forms of people, wearing flowing linen and other natural fabrics.  It’s a festival and potluck of the grandest proportions–just about to get rolling with all kinds of homemade and had grown food.  Children are running around, roaming in packs, laughing, singing, cackling.  Parents are talking and laughing–secure in knowing that their children will be well cared for by everyone – and easy to find.

Play – to be so in love with ourselves and one another that we can be and express and play. To have the vulnerability and humility to play in non-competitive ways, to not be afraid to be weird, fun, funky, expressive. Art is everywhere – We have a public space dedicated to the arts. We learn, teach and document with art. Queer artists will be celebrated and honored.

Culture continues to be preserved yet ever-evolving, hand in hand with art and creativity. We are learning new ways to repurpose the waste of our ancestors and the natural materials around us into beautiful, functional, sturdy and lasting things. Our fashion is a reflection of our innovation and ingenuity, our ability to transform waste into items worthy of our adornment.
Clothes are made from recycled textiles.

Safety, for people, for everyone, health , happiness, clean airi and water, unity, strength like the moutnains. Our song and dance continuing on. Our fluent language being spoken. Ceremony, what has kept us resilient and strong to carry on our stories. 7 generations ahead- we plan for that. It’s in us. Connection is always there. Language and health - what has been taken from us will be brought back.

Sacred moutnain- grass mountain- our people are displaced but also thriving. The current mindset, colonial mindset. Our sacred villages, which is now solvang, the items we cant have returned back. Musical items, songs have not been revitalized due to villages being excluded, bring back the songs, the stories. Prepare the youth so that they don’t  have to do the work we’re doing now.

Return back to the past way of life in a modern way. I respect where they got us. The last of us- post apocalyptic ways- in 150 yrs it could be us - return to what the old ones have taught us, farming cultural teachings in small pods like this. I’m in the past a lot bc of the things and places I get to see and what those places do for me in my spirit. We do things in 4’s- sing songs in 4’s, spirit is there, life is breathed into us, from the earth, lived experience and death and we all come back again. Like circular motion- cultural connectivity and continuity. The circular motion comes back to us.
Only 100% Organic cotton clothing. Polyester banned.
Planet earth healed and people are able to pour into art poetry, oral and written history, to explore and learn from others.
A statue of Ben (community coalition’s youth organizer.)

There would be a pro-kick ball league. A statue of Ben that is 15 foot high in a beautiful courtyard. Flying houses. The most important things that the statue of Ben and the kickball league. The League would be fun because we used to play in elementary and never again, and it would be amazing.
We recreate with fun sports.
They are singing the songs of our people. Lyrics about the strength, sights of what they saw along the way.
